summary_markdown:
No action is due off this report — it is retrospective, and the regret table below is the part most likely to be misread as a start/sit instruction. It is not one. Each row is an independent counterfactual against the same bench, so the same player can answer several rows, and the `gap` column does not add up. `optimal_lineup` is the one figure here that legitimately aggregates the week.

Against week 1 there is no prior to compare with, so nothing in this report describes a change; it describes a baseline. The scoring margins were wide enough that no single lineup decision flipped a result.

What this report cannot see: it knows nothing about injuries or usage after the window closed, it has no view of what the waiver wire will offer tomorrow, and a retrospective margin over a bench player says nothing about whether that player should start next week.
